title: Land organisms change faster than marine organisms

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Land organisms change faster than marine organisms

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Terrestrial organisms appear to change at a faster rate through geological time than marine organisms.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The productions of the land seem to change at a quicker rate than those of the sea, of which a striking instance has lately been observed in Switzerland.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter X, “On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings”; section “On their different rates of change”. Scope: terrestrial versus marine biotas in the fossil record

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch10-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The database supports direct environmental comparisons, but preservation creates a severe, directionally relevant confound. Restricted matched analyses are feasible; a global verdict is less secure.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare standardized origination, extinction, turnover, and morphological rates for matched terrestrial and marine clades and time bins. Support requires consistently higher rates on land after controlling for preservation, taxonomy, and clade composition.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Terrestrial preservation and sampling are much poorer than marine preservation.

'Change' can mean turnover or morphological evolution.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.78
discriminating power: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.68
data existence: 0.84
data adequacy: 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The land-versus-sea contrast maps cleanly onto environment-coded turnover, and both marine occurrences and Cenozoic land mammals are public. Coverage is adequate for a Cenozoic mammal-versus-marine comparison and poor for the full Phanerozoic scope. Preservation differences push in the same direction as the claim often enough that a raw rate gap would not be decisive.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare per-lineage origination, extinction, or morphological-change rates for terrestrial versus marine taxa over the same Phanerozoic intervals, after sampling standardization. Faster terrestrial change would support the claim; equal or slower terrestrial change would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Land fossils are rarer and more episodic than marine shells, which moves apparent rates even when biological rates are similar.

Environment is incompletely coded, and many important terrestrial groups have little pre-Cenozoic record.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.85
data existence: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.45
